title: U.S. Senate (special) · Florida

context.text: Special election to fill the remainder of the term Marco Rubio (R) was elected to in 2022, which expires in January 2029. Rubio resigned on January 20, 2025 after being confirmed as U.S. Secretary of State; Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) appointed Ashley Moody as his interim successor the next day. In the August 18, 2026 primaries, Moody defeated Chris Gleason, Ernie Rivera and Neelam Perry for the Republican nomination (79.6%), and Angela Nixon defeated Alex Vindman for the Democratic nomination (55.9%-44.1%).

candidates.name: Ashley Moody
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary with 79.6% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Senator from Florida (appointed January 2025; assumed office 2025)

summary.text: Ashley Moody is the incumbent Republican U.S. Senator from Florida, appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis in January 2025 to fill the seat vacated by Marco Rubio and now running to serve the remainder of the term through January 2029. She previously served as Florida Attorney General (2019-2025) and as a judge on Florida's 13th Judicial Circuit Court (2007-2017).

background.text: Earned bachelor's and master's degrees in accounting from the University of Florida, and law degrees from the University of Florida and Stetson University.
Worked as an attorney, law professor and federal prosecutor before seeking elected office.
Served as an elected judge on Florida's 13th Judicial Circuit Court from 2007 to 2017.
Served as Florida Attorney General from 2019 to 2025.
Appointed by Gov. Ron DeSantis to the U.S. Senate on January 21, 2025 to succeed Marco Rubio.

priorities.text: Says she is a supporter of President Trump's agenda and is 'dedicated to America First policies that promote law and order, economic prosperity, and American sovereignty.'
Campaigns on her record as Attorney General, citing efforts to 'enhance public safety, strengthen law enforcement, and crack down on violent crime.'
Describes herself as a national leader on 'protecting religious freedom and the sanctity of life.'

positions.summary: Is a cosponsor of the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act, which would let people with a concealed-carry privilege in their home state carry in other states that allow concealed carry.
positions.quote: I’m proud to cosponsor the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act

positions.summary: Introduced the Child Interstate Abortion Notification Act in January 2026, which would make it a federal offense to knowingly transport a minor across state lines without complying with parental consent and notification laws for abortion.
positions.quote: I’m introducing the Child Interstate Abortion Notification Act to strengthen protections for parents and families by ensuring compliance with state parental notification and consent laws.

positions.summary: Is a cosponsor of the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025, which would generally prohibit school athletic programs from allowing individuals whose biological sex at birth was male to participate in programs for women and girls.
positions.quote: Male athletes have no business competing in women's sports

candidates.name: Angela Nixon
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Alex Vindman, 55.9%-44.1%.

summary.text: Angela Nixon is a Democratic state representative from Jacksonville, a union organizer and small-business owner running for the remainder of the U.S. Senate term vacated by Marco Rubio. She has worked on legislation on childcare access and price-gouging and previously led the statewide coalition Florida for All.

background.text: Elected to the Florida House of Representatives in 2022.
Worked as a union organizer and runs a community-focused bookstore in Jacksonville.
Previously led the statewide coalition Florida for All.
In the Florida House, worked on legislation expanding childcare access, addressing price-gouging, and challenging Florida's voting maps.

priorities.text: Lowering everyday costs amid what she calls an affordability crisis, including housing and insurance costs.
priorities.quote: Floridians are being crushed by an affordability crisis created by greed and corruption.

priorities.text: Creating a healthcare system that works for everyone and protecting Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid and the VA.

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page calls for Medicare for All covering every person in America.
positions.quote: Medicare for All that covers every person in America — free at the point of service, with no premiums, no deductibles, no copays, and no surprise bills.

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page calls for universal, high-quality child care and pre-kindergarten for every family regardless of income.
positions.quote: Universal, high-quality child care and pre-kindergarten for every family, regardless of income

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page lists protecting reproductive freedom, including the right to abortion.
positions.quote: the right to abortion, contraception, and IVF, free from political interference

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page calls for abolishing ICE, a moratorium on deportations pending an audit of enforcement practices, and ending mass deportation.
positions.quote: mass incarceration and mass deportation are moral failures, and I will fight in the United States Senate to end them.

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page calls for a 5% annual wealth tax on billionaires and for closing corporate tax loopholes.
positions.quote: A 5% annual wealth tax on billionaires.

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page calls for a union-built transition to renewable energy and for ending taxpayer subsidies for fossil fuel corporations.
positions.quote: A bold, union-built transition to renewable energy

positions.summary: Her campaign priorities page calls for raising the federal minimum wage to a living wage indexed to inflation.
positions.quote: Raising the federal minimum wage to a real living wage, indexed to inflation

record.text: As a Florida state representative, worked on legislation expanding childcare access and addressing price-gouging.

candidates.name: Neil Gillespie

summary.text: Neil Gillespie is a no-party-affiliation candidate running for U.S. Senate in Florida's special election. He has also run for President of the United States (2020, and declared for 2028) and for Governor of Florida in 2026, but did not appear on that gubernatorial ballot.

candidates.researchNotes: Gillespie did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and no campaign website content or public statements on issues could be located; he has not previously held elected office.
